author: ohtadmin
title: North Road utility project set to start
text:
Rhode Island Energy for the last 18 months has been experiencing the painstaking task of replacing its utility poles throughout Jamestown.
So far, it’s been unnoticeable “in most cases,” said Town Administrator Ed Mello.
That inconspicuous undertaking, however, is about to become obvious.
“They have a project that will be very noticeable,” he said.
Mello briefed the town council about the project at its Oct. 6 meeting. He said the utility company currently is surveying and excavating on North Road as it prepares to replace every pole from Narragansett Avenue to Weeden Lane. Mello expects the project to be “very frustrating for people” who routinely traverse that route.
“It takes a long time,” he said. “It takes years for this work to get done.”
The main reason for the drawn-out timetable, according to Mello, is due to infrastructure on the poles that is not owned by Rhode Island Energy. Verizon, Cox and the fire department, for example, have equipment installed on these poles.
“All of that coordination takes a long time,” he said.
Mello also said the historical significance of Indian burial grounds with the environmental sensitivity of the Great Creek add a degree of caution to the project.
“I suggest they are going to be very slow and deliberate,” he said.
Council Vice President Erik Brine asked whether Rhode Island Energy considered burying the lines.
“They do not bury utility lines as a matter of practices,” Mello replied. “They actually avoid it for a lot of reasons.”
The primary reason is that burying lines is more expensive. Mello said there are cities and towns that have entered into agreements with utility companies to bury their lines. Most of these agreements, however, cost the community “millions of dollars” to offset the final number.
Mello said Rhode Island Energy also avoids underground lines because repairing them is “significantly more difficult,” which slows down their response times.
“They are not a fan of underground utilities,” he said.
— Tim Riel
